whatIs.title: What is the Loan Calculator?
whatIs.description: Enter the loan amount, rate and term to compare monthly payments and total interest across equal installment, equal principal and bullet repayment. You can also add a grace period, find the maximum loan for a monthly budget, see how payments move with rate changes, and run a quick DSR check.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter the loan amount, annual rate and term — results appear immediately.
2. Pick a repayment method (equal installment / equal principal / bullet) and a grace period.
3. In the 'Monthly → max loan' tab, enter what you can pay each month to see the maximum you can borrow.
4. Use the comparison table, rate-change table and DSR check below; open the repayment schedule calculator for the full month-by-month table.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Even 0.1%p matters: for KRW 300M over 30 years (equal installment, around 4%), total interest differs by about KRW 6M, so compare lenders.
Equal principal has the lowest total interest but higher early payments — choose it if you have room in your early budget.
Manage your credit score (no late payments, moderate card utilization) to lower the spread on your rate.
If you choose a variable rate, check the 'What if the rate changes?' table to make sure you can handle a 1–2%p rise.
Prepaying early saves the most interest. Prepayment fees usually stop after 3 years.

items.q: Equal installment or equal principal — which is better?
items.a: Equal principal costs less total interest but has higher early payments. Choose equal principal if you have early cash flow, or equal installment for a steady monthly payment.

items.q: What is a grace period loan?
items.a: You pay only interest for a set period, then repay principal and interest over the remaining term. It lowers early payments but increases total interest because principal is repaid later.

items.q: If I can pay KRW 1.5M a month, how much can I borrow?
items.a: Use the 'Monthly → max loan' tab. For example, at 4.5% over 30 years with equal installment it is about KRW 296M. Actual limits can be lower due to DSR/LTV rules and bank review.

items.q: What is DSR and how does the 40% rule apply?
items.a: DSR is the ratio of annual principal + interest on all loans to annual income. When total loans exceed KRW 100M, banks cap it at 40% and non-bank lenders at 50%, and variable-rate loans are assessed with an added stress rate. The DSR here is for reference only.

items.q: How do LTV and DTI affect a loan?
items.a: LTV limits the loan relative to collateral value; DTI limits annual repayment relative to income. Lower ratios mean higher limits and better rates.

items.q: When is the prepayment fee waived?
items.a: Most prepayment fees are waived 3 years after the loan starts. Government policy loans may differ, so check with your bank.
